individuals.cause_of_death: cerebral hemorrhage (passed away with the clinical picture of cerebral hemorrhage, after 25 days comatose)
individuals.treatment_summary: Packed cells and platelets transfused at another center; methylprednisolone pulse therapy (30 mg/kg, three doses in 3 days), intravenous etoposide (5 mg/kg/dose, three doses) and oral cyclosporine (5 mg/kg/day); discharged on oral dexamethasone and cyclosporine. At 2 years 4 months receiving etoposide every 2 weeks, oral dexamethasone and cotrimoxazole syrup (treatment never stopped since 4 months). Etanercept prescribed after WES but never started (family did not initiate, apparently due to cost).

individuals.treatment_summary: Etoposide, dexamethasone and cyclosporine A per HLH Guideline 2004, plus a course of ganciclovir; after the genetic result, etanercept 0.8 mg/kg per week subcutaneously with cyclosporine A and corticosteroid gradually discontinued; now etanercept every 2 weeks, completely symptom-free.
individuals.disease_label_as_stated: HA20 due to TNFAIP3 mutation, primarily manifested with HLH (authors suggest HLH/MAS); familial HLH initially 'confirmed' before WES
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Provisional HLH diagnosis from fever, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, hypoalbuminemia, hypertriglyceridemia and hypofibrinogenemia; trio WES (NovaSeq 6000, SureSelect V6-Post, 100X) found a heterozygous de novo TNFAIP3 variant, confirmed by Sanger sequencing

variants.variant_original_string: c. T824C in exon 6, p. L275P
variants.parental_testing_statement: WES performed on DNA of the patient and his parents; Sanger sequencing confirmed the patient is heterozygous for this de novo mutation, while his parents are homozygous wild type
variants.functional_evidence_statement: No functional assay reported. In silico only: CADD score 29.1; SIFT and PolyPhen-2 predicted the variant as probably deleterious; not reported in HGMD or ClinVar Miner. Text describes it as a proline to leucine change (p. L275P).
